title: Model
spec:
Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. This ensures that the model is aligned with the global coordinate system. Next, draw the first two-dimensional sketch on the first face. For the first loop, draw a line from the origin (0.0, 0.0) to (0.3409, 0.3409), then from (0.3409, 0.3409) to (0.0, 0.3409), and finally back to the origin. For the second loop, draw a line from (0.0341, 0.0823) to (0.2586, 0.3068), then from (0.2586, 0.3068) to (0.0341, 0.3068), and back to (0.0341, 0.0823).

On the second face, draw another two-dimensional sketch. For the first loop, draw a line from (0.0, 0.3409) to (0.3409, 0.3409), then from (0.3409, 0.3409) to (0.3409, 0.75), from (0.3409, 0.75) to (0.2898, 0.75), and finally back to (0.0, 0.3409). For the second loop, draw a line from (0.0659, 0.375) to (0.3068, 0.375), then from (0.3068, 0.375) to (0.3068, 0.7151), and back to (0.0659, 0.375).

After completing the sketches, apply a scale factor of 0.75 to the entire sketch to adjust the size. Then, transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional model by rotating it using Euler angles of 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 and translating it using a translation vector of 0.0, 0.0, 0.0. Finally, extrude the sketch 0.0102 units in the direction of the normal to create a new solid body. Ensure that the extrusion does not extend in the opposite direction of the normal. The final dimensions of the model will be a length of 0.3409, a width of 0.75, and a height of 0.0102.

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the triangular base
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.3409, 0.3409) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.3409) \
     .close()

# Define the inner loop for the base
r = r.moveTo(0.0341, 0.0823) \
     .lineTo(0.2586, 0.3068) \
     .lineTo(0.0341, 0.3068) \
     .close()

# Define the rectangular top
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.3409) \
     .lineTo(0.3409, 0.3409) \
     .lineTo(0.3409, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.2898, 0.75) \
     .close()

# Define the inner loop for the top
r = r.moveTo(0.0659, 0.375) \
     .lineTo(0.3068, 0.375) \
     .lineTo(0.3068, 0.7151) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.0102)

lanes.label: GLM-5.3 Flash (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Plate thickness (Z)
t = 0.0102

# Outer boundary of the flat plate (top view profile), points in XY
outer_pts = [
    (0.2865, 0.75),   # top edge left end
    (0.3409, 0.75),   # top edge right end
    (0.3409, 0.337),  # right point (middle band)
    (0.0084, 0.0),    # bottom point
    (0.0, 0.337),     # left point (middle band)
]

# Upper triangular cutout
upper_hole = [
    (0.0843, 0.379),
    (0.3034, 0.708),
    (0.3034, 0.379),
]

# Lower triangular cutout
lower_hole = [
    (0.0388, 0.312),
    (0.2190, 0.312),
    (0.0388, 0.0843),
]

# Base plate
base = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .polyline(outer_pts)
    .close()
    .extrude(t)
)

# Upper triangular hole
cut1 = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .polyline(upper_hole)
    .close()
    .extrude(t)
)

# Lower triangular hole
cut2 = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .polyline(lower_hole)
    .close()
    .extrude(t)
)

# Final part
r = base.cut(cut1).cut(cut2)

lanes.label: Kimi K3 (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

W = 0.3409
H = 0.7500
T = 0.0102
b = 0.0227

outer = [
    (0.0, 0.0),
    (0.0, 0.5),
    (2 * W / 3, H),
    (W, H),
    (W, 0.5),
]

upper_hole = [
    (0.1322, 0.5 + b),
    (W - b, 0.5 + b),
    (W - b, H - b),
]

lower_hole = [
    (b, 0.1440),
    (b, 0.5 - b),
    (0.2500, 0.5 - b),
]

r = cq.Workplane("XY").polyline(outer).close().extrude(T)
r = r.faces(">Z").workplane().polyline(upper_hole).close().cutThruAll()
r = r.faces(">Z").workplane().polyline(lower_hole).close().cutThruAll()
